summary: A limestone tower on the Labrador shore of the Strait of Belle Isle, lit in 1858, kept by the Wyatt family for generations and neighbour to the 1922 wreck of HMS Raleigh.

access.note: Provincial Historic Site; open in season, closed for the winter.

notes_for_editor: Lighthouse Friends dates the HMS Raleigh grounding 8 August 1902; the Department of Marine report for 1923-24, SPSNL and Parks Canada all give 1922, which the story follows. LF says ten sailors drowned; Parks Canada says eleven died, SPSNL says 11 of 797. The story uses the Parks Canada figure. Keeper dates disagree between the station website and LF (see roster notes). LF says the lighthouse is owned by the Canadian Coast Guard; the record says provincial; the story says only Provincial Historic Site. Keeper table 1904-05: Wyatt's appointment date matched by column position (OCR prints columns as blocks). The OCR in the 1923-24 report reads 'Nordjjeld'; the story says Nordfjeld (probable Nordfjeld, unverified). The HMS Lily claim is the station website's only; not checked. The tower height 33 m comes from the station website; Parks Canada's 33.2 m figure was not readable in the cached pages. Not searched: newspapers, Rowlett, CCG current light list (characteristic Oc W 20s kept from record only). The site website says 132 steps, provincial page says 128 and 132; omitted. Fact-check 2026-10-27: Department report volumes are labelled by fiscal year ended (1902v36=June 1901, 1904v38=June 1903, 1905v39=June 1904, 1906v40=June 1905, 19061907v41=June 1906, 1924v60=March 1923); story footnotes corrected. Wyatt's 1889 date confirmed on the page image (printed p.158, one line). Ice notes read on the page image (printed p.27, all Point Amour). Marconi year 1904 rests on Lighthouse Friends, since the report gives only '10 August'.
